title: Evaluation of condensed scalar extensions on w-contractible affines
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$, and let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $Q\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put
$$L_T(Q)=\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline Q\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T),$$
using ordinary derived tensor in module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], constant sheaves with discrete coefficients, and the canonical constant-section map $\underline R\to\Lambda_T$.

Let $V\to T$ be a pro-etale object with $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Thus $A$ is w-strictly local and its connected-component space $S=\pi_0(V)$, with the quotient topology, is an extremally disconnected profinite set (the closure of every open is open). There are natural ring and derived-module isomorphisms
$$\Gamma(V,\Lambda_V)\cong\Gamma(S,\Lambda),\qquad
R\Gamma(V,L_T(Q)|_V)\cong Q\otimes^L_R\Gamma(S,\Lambda).$$
The functor $R\Gamma(V,-):D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_V)\to D(\Gamma(S,\Lambda))$ is t-exact for the standard t-structures. The displayed comparisons are natural in $Q$. No t-admissibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 3, equations (3.1), (3.2) and Remark 3.2; Lemma 4.1(1); Proposition 4.3(1), which identifies coefficient sections through the component-site map. The extremal disconnectedness is Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.4.8, also explicitly invoked in the proof of Theorem 6.2.

proof.text: Put $B=\Gamma(V,\Lambda_T)$. The geometric w-contractibility in the hypothesis gives weak contractibility of the site object $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-source-affine-wcontractible-evaluation]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-point-basis-evaluation] with $X=T$, $U=V$ and $F=\Lambda$: it gives $B\cong\Lambda(S)=\Gamma(S,\Lambda)$ as rings. This comparison is natural and respects the constant-section maps from $R=\Lambda(*)$, since those maps are induced by the unique map $S\to *$. Extremal disconnectedness of $S$ is already part of the stated meaning of w-contractibility [sk-def-pe-wlocal].

source.place: Proposition 4.3(1), proof equation (4.2), and proof of (3); Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.4.8

proof.text: By [det-pe-wc-sections-exact], evaluation of $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves at $V$ is exact; by [det-pe-wc-sections-derived] its termwise application to any unbounded complex computes $R\Gamma(V,-)$. Explicitly exactness identifies $\Gamma(V,\ker d^n)$ and $\Gamma(V,\operatorname{im}d^{n-1})$ with the kernel and image of the section differential, hence $H^n\Gamma(V,C)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^n C)$. A complex with cohomology sheaves zero above, or below, a given degree therefore has section cohomology zero in the same range. This proves t-exactness. Moreover [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-wcontractible-affine-evaluation-colimits] applies because $V$ is affine and weakly contractible by step 1; evaluation preserves all small colimits.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(1), proof: t-exactness and colimit preservation of sections on a w-contractible qcqs object

proof.text:
For an ordinary $R$-module $M$ set $F(M)=\Lambda_T\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$. Consider the global-sections geometric morphism $\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}})\to\mathrm{Set}$, whose inverse image is the constant-sheaf functor, with structural ring map $\underline R\to\Lambda_T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], $F$ is its module pullback, so is left adjoint to sections with scalars restricted to $R$. Thus $F$ preserves coproducts and cokernels: mapping out of $F(\operatorname{colim}M_i)$ gives the compatible families of maps from $M_i$ to the right adjoint, which are exactly the maps out of $\operatorname{colim}F(M_i)$. By step 2, $M\mapsto\Gamma(V,F(M))$ also preserves these colimits. The functor $M\mapsto M\otimes_R B$ does so by the balanced-tensor universal property. The natural balanced map
$$\theta_M:M\otimes_R B\longrightarrow\Gamma(V,F(M)),\qquad m\otimes b\longmapsto b(1\otimes\underline m),$$
is $B$-linear, and $\theta_R$ is the identity of $B$ under the unit identifications.

source.place: Remark 3.2, ordinary scalar-extension model; adjunction is Stacks Tag 03D7, sites-modules lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules

proof.text: For every set $I$, $\theta_{R^{(I)}}$ is the direct sum of copies of $\theta_R$, so is an isomorphism. For any $M$ choose a free presentation $R^{(J)}\to R^{(I)}\to M\to0$: take generators indexed by elements of $M$, and relations indexed by elements of the kernel of the resulting surjection. Apply both cokernel-preserving functors of step 3. Naturality of $\theta$ identifies their presentation arrows, and the already established isomorphisms on the two free modules induce an isomorphism on their cokernels. Consequently $\theta_M$ is an isomorphism for every $M$, without assuming $B$ flat over $R$.

source.place: Equation (3.2) and Remark 3.2, degree-zero comparison expanded by free presentations

proof.text: Represent $Q\in D(R)$ by a complex $A$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-object point site with coefficient ring $R$ to choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to A$ with $P$ K-flat and with flat terms. Pullback along the global-sections geometric morphism with coefficient ring $\underline R$ sends $P$ to $\underline P$, which is K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. By [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], the constant-module functor is exact and its termwise application induces $\underline{(-)}$ on unbounded derived categories; thus $\underline P\to\underline A$ is a quasi-isomorphism representing $\underline Q$. Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to $\underline R\to\Lambda_T$. The complex $C=\Lambda_T\otimes_{\underline R}\underline P$, with differential $1\otimes d_P$, represents $L_T(Q)$. Apply the same change-of-rings result on the point site to $R\to B$: $P\otimes_R B$ represents $Q\otimes_R^L B$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YT and 06YY (derived change of rings); HRS Remark 3.2

proof.text:
By [det-pe-wc-sections-derived], $R\Gamma(V,L_T(Q))$ is represented by the section complex $C(V)$. Apply $\theta_{P^n}$ from step 4 in each degree. Naturality for $d_P^n:P^n\to P^{n+1}$ gives a chain isomorphism $P\otimes_R B\xrightarrow{\sim}C(V)$. Step 5 identifies its source with $Q\otimes_R^L B$. Invert this chain isomorphism and use the ring comparison of step 1. This gives
$$R\Gamma(V,L_T(Q))\cong Q\otimes_R^L\Gamma(S,\Lambda).$$
No interchange of an infinite totalization with sections, and no boundedness or flatness assumption on $B$, is used.

source.place: Equation (3.2) and Remark 3.2, computed on unbounded K-flat representatives

proof.text: The chain maps $\theta_{P^n}$ commute with every chain map $P\to P'$ by their displayed pure-tensor formula. The resolution comparisons for scalar extension are compatible with quasi-isomorphisms and composition by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The K-flat, flat-term representatives localized at quasi-isomorphisms are all of $D(R)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], applied to the point site. Therefore the chain comparison descends to a natural isomorphism for every morphism of $D(R)$, not just chain maps in one selected resolution. The coefficient ring comparison is natural by step 1.

source.place: Tags 06YT, 06YY and 06YS; localization of K-flat representatives, as in the construction of derived tensor; HRS equations (3.1)–(3.2)

proof.text: Finally [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with the slice $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$. The exact restriction of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction] evaluates a complex on an object $W\to V$ by its original value on $W\to T$; at the terminal object $V\to V$ its section complex is precisely $C(V)$. The pulled-back coefficient sheaf restricts to $\Lambda_V$ by functoriality of inverse image in [def-sfb-alpha-bundled]. Thus the sections in steps 2 and 6 are exactly $R\Gamma(V,L_T(Q)|_V)$ with coefficient ring $\Gamma(V,\Lambda_V)$. Steps 1, 2 and 6–7 prove every asserted comparison and t-exactness. None used t-admissibility.

source.place: Section 3, functoriality of coefficient pullback and equation (3.2); Lemma 4.1(1); Stacks localized ringed-site restriction
